episode_title: From 200 to 2,000 Closings: Boyd Martin, former Division President, D.R. Horton Utah
question: How did D.R. Horton Utah scale from 200 closings to 2,000 annual closings under Boyd Martin?
transcript_excerpt: Boyd Martin grew the D.R. Horton Utah division from about 200 homes per year when he became division president in early 2004 to 2,001 closings, making it the largest home builder in Utah for four consecutive years. He attributed this growth to lessons learned from Rick Salisbury on production efficiency, low overhead management, and promoting talent from within the organization—the average tenure of his executive team was about 14 years, with everyone except the in-house counsel promoted from within.

episode_title: From 200 to 2,000 Closings: Boyd Martin, former Division President, D.R. Horton Utah
question: What was Rick Salisbury's 45-day construction schedule method and why did it work?
transcript_excerpt: Rick Salisbury built homes in 45 calendar days, start to finish, with a simple one-page fax schedule sent to vendors specifying exact start and completion dates. The schedule had nothing to do with technology but everything to do with mindset: vendors knew if they started Monday morning, they had to be done by the specified day because another crew was arriving at 6 a.m. the next morning. Salisbury hit this 45-day schedule 99% of the time by maintaining strict discipline and coordination among trades.

episode_title: From 200 to 2,000 Closings: Boyd Martin, former Division President, D.R. Horton Utah
question: What was Rick Salisbury's pricing and commission strategy that made Salisbury Homes competitive?
transcript_excerpt: Rick Salisbury never paid buyer's agent commission (BAC)—he took the standard 3% buyer's agent commission at that time and dropped it off the home's price instead. Combined with his negotiated low vendor prices and overhead of only 3-3.6%, Salisbury was able to maintain gross margins of 10-13% while undercutting competitors, making his homes appear cheaper while actually maintaining strong profitability.

episode_title: From 200 to 2,000 Closings: Boyd Martin, former Division President, D.R. Horton Utah
question: How did D.R. Horton's founder D.R. Horton start the company and what made him different from Rick Salisbury?
transcript_excerpt: D.R. Horton founded his company in 1978 with just three homes, doing everything himself and selling them himself. He became the largest home builder in the country within 24 years. While both Rick Salisbury and D.R. Horton started around the same time with similar bootstrapping approaches, they treated people differently, but both were instrumental mentors who taught Boyd Martin lessons on operational excellence and long-term success.

episode_title: From 200 to 2,000 Closings: Boyd Martin, former Division President, D.R. Horton Utah
question: What percentage of the homebuilding market did the top 10 builders control in the 1990s versus today?
transcript_excerpt: In the 1990s, the top 10 builders controlled only about 10% of the market, whereas today they control 40 to 50% of the market. Back in 1998-2000, the market was much more diversified and local, dominated by independent and regional builders, with public companies like KB Holmes and Pulte pulling out of markets like Utah due to poor margins.
